title: Corso says The Day After Roswell was rushed to print
summary: James Fox tells of Corso says The Day After Roswell was rushed to print, about 1997 at Roswell, New Mexico, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he said that they rushed the book to print with William Burns
No. No. Rumor has it he only had 24 hours to edit it. And according to his son, he put his hand to his head and said, "I I can't believe this."
tellings.difference: Adds the rumour that he had only 24 hours to edit it and his son's account of his dismayed reaction.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell that The Day After Roswell was rushed to print in 1997 without Corso being able to edit it properly.

as_told.title: Corso had 24 hours to edit The Day After Roswell

plain: James Fox tells podcast host Jesse Michels about The Day After Roswell, a 1997 book by Philip J. Corso about events at Roswell, New Mexico. Fox passes on that Corso said the book was rushed into print with a co-writer named William Burns, and he also mentions a man named Michael Hessman. If true, the rush might explain problems in the book without throwing out what Corso claimed.
